title: AWS Bedrock AgentCore install_packages -- T1059 unescaped extras group smuggles shell metacharacters into a pip install command
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-16796 (GHSA-j6g5-3hh3-pgw8),
affecting the AWS Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK (`bedrock-agentcore`)
Code Interpreter client prior to 1.18.1.

`install_packages()` in `code_interpreter_client.py` validated each
package specifier against `VALID_PACKAGE_NAME`, but the extras-group
portion of that regex was `(\[.*\])?` -- any characters at all inside
the brackets. A specifier like `requests[$(id)]` or
`` flask[`whoami`] `` passed validation, and because the vulnerable
code joined the accepted specifiers with plain `" ".join(packages)`
(no shell quoting) before building `pip install <specifiers>` and
handing it to `executeCommand`, the bracket content reached a shell
intact -- command substitution inside the extras group executes
arbitrary commands inside the Code Interpreter sandbox. The fix
tightened the extras-group pattern to `[a-zA-Z0-9._,\-]*` (valid pip
extra names only) and added `shlex.quote()` around every specifier
before joining.

Detection logic flags an `install_packages` / `executeCommand`
invocation whose package specifier's extras-group brackets contain a
shell metacharacter -- `$(`, a backtick, a semicolon, or a bare space
-- the exact injection shape the fix's regression tests
(`requests[$(id)]`, `` flask[`whoami`] ``, `pandas[a b c]`) name.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (AWS, via
GHSA and NVD) plus the actual pre/post-fix source diff (commit
`3c4b4ee6`, PR #581) confirming the exact vulnerable regex and the
missing `shlex.quote()`, fixed in 1.18.1.
